messages.subject: Robustness of spatially explicit JSSA models
messages.subject_clean: Robustness of spatially explicit JSSA models
messages.body_plain:
I am using an open secr model (PLBsecrl) to estimate phi and lambda across a number of years.  I also have estimates of abundance using a closed secr model, from which I can estimate lambda by hand.  I want to say that the PLBsecrl model is more robust to assumption violations (e.g., non-homogenous capture probabilities) than the closed secr model for estimating lambda, because N (which is greatly affected by such assumption violations) does not enter into the equation in the latter.  The Efford and Schofield (2020) paper seems to say this but I just wanted to make sure I am reading that correctly.  Thanks for any feedback!
Joe

messages.subject: Re: Robustness of spatially explicit JSSA models
messages.subject_clean: Robustness of spatially explicit JSSA models
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe

I'm not sure this is right. I can't put my finger on where the 2020 paper that might support what you suggest.

Closed-population multi-session analyses can get quite sophisticated - have you seen https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-trend.pdf?

A relevant non-spatial paper is Hines & Nichols (2002) 'Investigations of potential bias in the estimation of lambda using Pradel's (1996) model for capture-recapture
data' Journal of Applied Statistics, 29:1-4, 573-587. That makes the point that for non-spatial CR, N-hat and therefore lambda-hat is sensitive to extent of sampling - this is one benefit of using SECR, whether open- or closed-.

Murray

messages.subject_clean: Robustness of spatially explicit JSSA models
messages.body_plain:
The comment that I was referring to was "The spatial open-population model relaxes some assumptions of non-spatial open-population and spatial closed-population models (Table 4). This enables parameters of interest (population growth rate ⁠, survival rate  and density ⁠) to be estimated with less bias and better confidence interval coverage (Table 4)."  The table then shows some of the biases of other models (including spatially explicit closed).  However, I think I see now that you were referring to the reduction of capture heterogeneity based on the spatial location of the activity centers would produce a more robust estimate than the non-spatially explicit estimate.
I had not seen the note on estimating lambda directly in closed secr models.  That is exactly what I need!  Thank you.
Joe

messages.subject: SECR code for adding multiple mask covariates
messages.subject_clean: SECR code for adding multiple mask covariates
messages.body_plain:
My experience in R is very limited and I am currently trying to develop SECR density models for wild turkeys on 3 wildlife management areas. Specifically I would like to use multiple habitat covariates( in the form of rasters), such as distance to nearest road and distance to nearest food plot, in a single model.
I am assuming this is possible from the reading I have done so far.
Does anyone have example code for adding multiple covariates they would be willing to share?
Hopefully my questions are clear.  Any help or suggestions would be appreciated

messages.subject: Re: SECR code for adding multiple mask covariates
messages.subject_clean: SECR code for adding multiple mask covariates
messages.body_plain:
Welcome to the group!
The brushtail possum example in secr-densitysurfaces.pdf <https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-densitysurfaces.pdf> shows how you can use the addCovariates() function to transfer covariates from a spatial data source to the habitat mask used in 'secr'. The source there is a polygon coverage, but you can also use rasters. You might also check secr-spatialdata.pdf <https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-spatialdata.pdf>. Once you have covariates in the habitat mask they can be named in the density model e.g. D~forestcover. Don't expect too much - - it works best with few covariates.
Murray

messages.subject: Re: SECR code for adding multiple mask covariates
messages.subject_clean: SECR code for adding multiple mask covariates
messages.body_plain:
No further thoughts, or at least none I can back up with evidence. My sense is that SECR datasets often contain little information about spatial pattern in activity centres (AC), perhaps because there is uncertainty regarding the true location of each AC. In consequence, stratum-specific estimates of density tend to have wide CI. Your mileage may vary.

messages.subject: secrapp 2.0 - spatially explicit capture-recapture in a GUI
messages.subject_clean: secrapp 2.0 - spatially explicit capture-recapture in a GUI
messages.body_plain:
The Shiny application 'secrapp' has been updated for secr 5.1 and is available at https://www.stats.otago.ac.nz/secrapp/, no installation required. Changes are mostly minor.

See GitHub <https://github.com/MurrayEfford/secrapp> for the development version, and check out the step-by-step guide <https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secrapp-tutorial.html>. Please report bugs as Issues on GitHub - after checking they are reproducible.
